The Erasmus School of History, Culture and Communication (ESHCC) is looking for two highly motivated PhD candidates to join a research group led by Dr. Natália da Silva Perez examining how European colonial expansion (1600-1900) influenced ideas about women's work. This research project combines archival research and computational text analysis of ideas on gendered labour across different transimperial locales. Your PhD research will focus on one of the project's historical cases to examine how women's lived experiences conformed to, or diverged from, normative ideas about gendered labour circulating between colonies and European metropoles.

 The function

You analyze user queries, resolve technical and functional issues, and contribute to improvements that make our processes more efficient and reliable. 
You combine your technical knowledge with insight into our production processes. You work on changes and projects, support implementations, and translate user needs into concrete improvements in our applications. Additionally, you monitor market developments and new technologies to ensure our systems remain future-proof. The key components of your role: - Application management of ERP/MES systems - Analysis of user queries and resolution of technical issues - Contribute to projects and changes - Implementing improvements in functionality and processes - Translating developments into system adjustments 
 Your strength 
Do you have a passion for IT, data, and business processes, and are you eager to learn, analytical, and a strong communicator? We are looking for someone who enjoys bridging the gap between technology and users and gets energy from improving systems. In addition, you bring the following: - HBO working and thinking level (HBO graduates are welcome) - Good command of Dutch and English - Basic knowledge of ERP or MES and an interest in production processes - Technical skills such as SQL, scripting, or PowerShell - Affinity with production IT and process optimization
